anomalies.observed: Four 0 Ω jumpers (R23, R6, R14, R8) are all populated. R23 and R6 both connect to NET0032, so bus pins 19 and 21 are tied together. R14 and R8 both connect to NET0021, so bus pins 20 and 22 are tied together. Each pair's two pins are shorted on the same net.
anomalies.expected: The specification says the jumper set is mutually exclusive: 'Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others'. Only one jumper per channel should be shorted to select pin 19/21 (ch.1) or pin 20/22 (ch.2). Shorting both pins of a pair would bridge two bus GPIOs.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2
Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others

anomalies.impact: If both jumpers in a pair are fitted, one PWM output drives two bus GPIOs at once. On a core where one of those pins has another function, this causes contention or a short and can disrupt the servo signal or the core's other peripherals.

parsed.summary: Most of the netlist matches the specification's topology and values, including the MAX3485 wiring, the battery and 5V paths, and the servo rail. The one concern is that all four bus-pin jumpers are populated, so each channel's two candidate GPIO pins are shorted together, which the spec's mutually-exclusive jumper scheme does not allow. Reference designators differ from the spec, so this is only moderately confident.
